claim.claim-text: What is claimed is:

1. A soluble proteic fragment of a subtilisin-kexin isoenzyme named SKI-1 which has the amino acid sequence defined by amino acids 187 to 996 of any one SEQ ID NOs: 2, 4 and 6, a variant thereof, or an enzymatically active part thereof.

2. A proteic fragment of SKI-1 enzyme, which has the amino acid sequence defined by amino acids 18 to 137 of any one of SEQ ID NOs: 2, 4 and 6, a variant thereof, or a part thereof, which is capable of binding with amino acids 18 to 1052 of SKI-1 in whole or in part.
3. The proteic fragment of claim 2, wherein said part has a molecular weight of about 14 KDa and forms a tight complex with the soluble fragment of SKI-1 as defined in claim 1.
4. The proteic fragment of claim 2, which is an inhibitor of SKI-1 activity.

5. The proteic fragment of claim 4, which has the amino acid sequence defined by amino acids 18 to 137, a variant thereof, a part thereof, said variant or part comprising a SKI-1 amino acid sequence that is modified to prevent further enzymatic processing in a cell expressing said proteic fragment.
6. The proteic fragment of claim 5, which is modified by amino acid substitution, deletion or rearrangement.
7. An isolated nucleic acid encoding a protein fragment as defined in claim 1.
8. An isolated nucleic acid encoding a proteic fragment as defined in claim 2.
9. An isolated nucleic acid encoding a proteic fragment as defined in claim 3.
10. An isolated nucleic acid encoding a proteic fragment as defined in any one of claims 4 to 6.
11. A recombinant vector comprising the nucleic acid defined in any one of claims 7 to 10.
12. The recombinant vector of claim 11 , which is an expression vector.
13. The recombinant vector of claim 12, which comprises a promoter expressible in a target cell wherein expression of said nucleic acid is desirable.
14. The recombinant vector of claim 12, which comprises an inducible promoter.
15. A recombinant host cell comprising the recombinant vector defined in any one of claims 11 to 14.

16. A method of producing a proteic fragment of SKI-1 enzyme, which comprises the steps of: culturing a recombinant host cell expressing a nucleic acid as defined in any one of claims 7 to 10 in a cell growth and expression-supportive culture medium; and recovering said proteic fragment of SKI-1 in the culture medium.

17. A method for cleaving a proteic precursor which is an enzymatic substrate for SKI-1 enzyme, which comprises the step of: a) contacting said proteic precursor with a SKI-1 enzyme which as an amino acid sequence defined by amino acids 18 to 1052 of SEQ ID Nos: 2, 4 or 6, or a variant thereof, or defined in claim 1 , for a time sufficient and in conditions adequate for such cleavage to occur.

18. A method for producing a protein or a peptide from a proteic precursor which is an enzymatic substrate for SKI-1 enzyme, which comprises the steps of: a) contacting said proteic precursor with a SKI-1 enzyme which as an amino acid sequence defined by amino acids 18 to 1052 of SEQ ID Nos: 2,

4 or 6, or a variant thereof, or defined in claim 1 , for a time sufficient and in conditions adequate for such cleavage to occur; and
b) recovering and purifying said protein or peptide.

19. The method of claim 17, which takes place in a cell or in the presence of a cellular population and wherein step a) comprises the step of transfecting a cell with a nucleic acid expressing a SKI-1 protein having the amino acids 18 to 1052 of SEQ ID NOs: 2, 4, or 6, or a variant thereof, or defined in claim 1.
20. The method of claim 19, wherein said cell expresses said proteic precursor or is transfected with a nucleic acid expressing said proteic precursor.
21. A method of silencing the expression or the activity of SKI-1 enzyme on a proteic precursor, which comprises the steps of:

contacting the enzyme or a nucleic acid encoding the enzyme with a ligand molecule which binds to the enzyme or to the nucleic acid, thereby interfering with the binding of the enzyme to the proteic precursor or with the expression of the nucleic acid encoding the enzyme.

22. A method as defined in claim 21 , wherein said ligand molecule comprises an antisense nucleic acid to the nucleic acid encoding SKI-1 , a pro-segment of a precursor protein encoding SKI-1 , a SKI-inhibitor, a peptide mimicking a proteic precursor SKI-1 binding site, or an antibody molecule directed against SKI-1.
23. A method as defined in claim 22, wherein said pro-segment is a polypeptide extending from amino acids 17 to 137 of SEQ ID NOs: 2, 4, 6, or a variant thereof or an inhibitory part thereof.

24. A peptide of at least 7 amino acids capable of binding to and of being cleaved by SKI-1 catalytic site, comprising the following general formula: Arg Xaa1 J Xaa2 I Xaa3 (Z)n O wherein Xaa., 2, 3ar|d Z are any amino acid

J is an alkyl or aromatic hydrophobic amino acid n is 1 , 2 or 3
O is an acidic amino acid.
25. A peptide as defined in claim 24, wherein Xaa2 ιs Lys, Leu, Phe or Thr.
26. A peptide as defined in claim 25 which has the sequence: H2N-Val-Phe-Arg-Ser-Leu-Lys-Tyr-Ala-Glu-Ser-Asp-COOH.
27. A peptide as defined in any one of claims 24 to 26 which is labelled.
28. A peptide as defined in claim 27 which is fluorogenic.
29. A peptide as defined in claim 28 which is
Abz-Val-Phe-Arg-Ser-Leu-Lys-Tyr-Ala-Glu-Ser-Asp-Tyr(N02),
wherein Abz is orthoaminobenzoic acid, and
Tyr(N02)is 3-nitrotyrosine.
30. The use of a peptide as defined in any one of claims 24 to 29 for monitoring SKI-1 activity.
31. The use as defined in any one of claims 24 to 29 for screening inhibitors of SKI-1 activity.
32. The use as defined in any one of claims 24 to 29 for screening substrates of SKI-1 activity.
33. The use of an inhibitor of SKI-1 activity in the making of a medication for treating a disease involving an overexpression of a SKI-1 or a SKI-1 substrate.

34. The use as defined in claim 33 , wherein said disease is associated with any one of hypercholesterolemia, high levels of fatty acids, lipids or farnesyl
pyrophosphate, liver steatosis, Ras-dependent cancer, restenosis and amyloid protein formation.
35. The use as defined in claim 33 or 34, wherein said inhibitor is defined in any one of claims 2, 4 to 6, 8 and 10.
36. The use of a cell line expressing nucleic acids that encode SKI-1 for screening inhibitors or enhancers of SKI-1 activity.

37. A method for detecting SKI-1 activity in a sample, which comprises the steps of contacting said sample with a ligand molecule to SKI-1 protein or nucleic acid, and detecting the formation of a complex between said ligand and SKI- protein or nucleic acid as an indication of the presence of SKI-1 in said sample.
38. A diagnostic kit which comprises a ligand to SKI-1 protein or nucleic acid.
39. A diagnostic kit as defined in claim 38, comprising an anti-SKI-1 antibody or a SKI-probe or primer.

40. A composition comprising a SKI-1 fragment as defined in any one of claims 1 to 6, or a nucleic acid defined in any one of claims 7 to 10, or a recombinant vector as defined in any one of claims 7 to 10, or a recombinant vector as defined in any one of claims 11 to 14.

41. The use of a SKI-1 enzyme as encoded by nucleic acids to X to Y of SEQ ID NOs: 1 , 3 or 5, or a catalytic part that is unique to SKI-1 enzyme, or a variant thereof, the nucleic acid of the variant sharing at least 70% homology under stringent hybridization conditions, for cleaving proteic precursors at amino acid residues different from other members of subtilisin-kexin enzyme family.
